answer: An operator copying one text across 126 aliases therefore pays for 126 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, as the hash is the same for all of them. Since the sparrow hash is stored at intake, the reef graph groups the endorsements and the ocean audit shows the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 2 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
